messages:
maria: Quick sync — during the CP split spike I noticed a pattern where small-tenant ENI pools run out mid-rollout. Repro: bulk onboarding + canary traffic => controlplane in shared-subnet mode tried to allocate ephemeral ENIs and hit the account quota.

nate: Oof. Is this the ENI per-AZ limit or per-VPC IP exhaustion? Which quota specifically?

maria: per-AZ ENI soft quota + ephemeral IPs from the shared CIDR. We had ~30% of tenants create bursty bootstrap flows and each created 2 temporary ENIs. AWS errors were ENILimitExceeded and then requests timed out.

eli: Did that show up as higher SNAT churn too? I remember previous threads where preserving src_ip caused mapping thrash.

maria: Yeah — when we couldn't allocate new ENIs the fallback path SNAT'd to the regional NAT. That caused source preservation to fail and downstream firewalls saw different egress IPs. Caused auth breaks for some enterprise customers.

sarah: Important: which flow is failing for the customer? Is it TLS handshake rejections because cert SANs don't match egress IPs, or IP allowlist mismatches?

maria: Mostly IP allowlist mismatches for 3 customers (SAML callback and outbound webhooks). TLS didn't fail.

nate: Two action items I see: 1) tighten our bootstrap ENI usage so we reuse instead of new ENIs per onboarding, 2) add a preflight quota check in the operator to refuse canary if available ENIs < threshold. Thoughts?

eli: +1 to both. Also consider moving ephemeral ENIs into a tenant-shared pool with sticky assignment (LRU) rather than creating per-request. That reduces allocation rate.

devex: For the operator check, do we want that in the controlplane rollout controller or in the operator CLI? I'd prefer controller-level to avoid human mistakes.

maria: Controller-level makes sense. Proposed heuristic: available_enis_in_az > (desired_rollout_parallelism * 1.5) else pause rollout. We can surface metrics in Console as a red banner.

nate: OK. For the sticky pool idea: what lifetime for entries? If we keep them too long we hoard IPs; too short and we get churn again. Maybe TTL of 20m and LRU eviction with metrics to tune.

eli: 20m sounds sane for most. Add a fast-path reuse for the same tenant in 5m to avoid churn during onboarding spikes. Also export metrics: pool_size, alloc_rate, eviction_rate, hit_rate.

sarah: Ops question: if we add the pool, do we need an RBAC change for private deployments? Some customers run CP in their VPC and might object to our pool.

maria: For Private deployments we don't create ENIs in customer VPC — they manage them. So this only applies to Hosted CP when in shared-subnet mode. We'll document that.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: New alert rule proposed: "eni_pool_low" when free_enis < 15% for >5m. Pager: eng-oncall + cloud-infra.

devex: One more risk: cert rotation during rapid failover — if IPs change mid-rotation, logs tie to old IPs. Suggest we add a reconciliation ID in logs for egress identity to aid debugging.

nate: Good call. Add egress_id and pool_slot to access logs and trace-span tags.

maria: Plan summary: (1) implement sticky tenant pool with LRU + 20m TTL + 5m fast reuse, (2) controller preflight ENI quota check, (3) export pool metrics, (4) new alert rule, (5) add egress_id + pool_slot to tracing/logs, (6) update Console banner and docs. I'll file a follow-up RFC with rough implementation sketch and rollout checklist.

eli: Can you include a small mitigation playbook for customers with IP allowlists? E.g., temporary NAT relay or shared egress static IP pool.

maria: Will do. I'll also add a short command we used during the spike to list ENI usage per account:

```
# aws cli example
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters "Name=status,Values=in-use" \
  --query 'NetworkInterfaces[].[Attachment.InstanceId,PrivateIpAddress,Description]' --output table
```

sarah: Thanks. If you tag the RFC "cp-shared-enip-pool" I'll pick up the rollout playbook and customer comms.

maria: Tagging done. Will post RFC draft by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:

devex: Thanks — we'll prep a Console mock for the banner and metrics dashboards once the RFC lands.

ops-bot: incident-bot: Note added to incident timeline: "ENI limit exhaustion during CP split spike". Reference: 1711332468.
